# Ellen West

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c2 P46](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0046), [v5 c13 P20](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0020)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Ellen  <sub>[v5 c2 P50](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0050), [v5 c4 P51](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0051), [v5 c12 P27](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0027)</sub>

## Appearance

Ellen West is ten years older than her sister Rosemary. She is dark and massive in build, with black hair, thick black eyebrows, and slaty-blue eyes.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P63](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0063), [v5 c13 P6](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0006), [v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008)_

## Personality

Ellen possesses a grim, stubborn, and outspoken nature, refusing to back down easily once her mind is made up. She has a jolly, gurgling laugh and an appreciation for sense and lively conversation. Underneath her stern exterior, she has a hearty laugh, a deep voice, and an interest in world affairs.

_Sources: [v5 c8 P29](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0029), [v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008), [v5 c13 P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027), [v5 c13 P37](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0037), [v5 c22 P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001)_

## Traits

- Stubborn
- Outspoken  <sub>[v5 c13 P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027)</sub>
- Fear of being left alone  <sub>[v5 c21 P20](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0020), [v5 c22 P31](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0031)</sub>

## Abilities

- Keen interest and knowledge in world politics and events  <sub>[v5 c13 P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027), [v5 c13 P29](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0029), [v5 c21 P9](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0009)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep her sister Rosemary from leaving her alone  <sub>[v5 c21 P20](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0020), [v5 c22 P31](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0031)</sub>

## History

Ellen West grew up as the elder daughter in the West family. In her youth, she was courted for two years by Norman Douglas, but the two parted after a sudden quarrel. Following her mother's death, Ellen suffered from deep grief and despondency, during which she exacted a solemn promise from her younger sister, Rosemary, that neither of them would ever marry so they could remain together. For years, Ellen and Rosemary lived quietly in the gray house on the hill, keeping out of local society. When Norman Douglas re-entered her life in her later years, he resumed his courtship. Ellen initially held Rosemary to her old vow, preventing Rosemary's marriage to Mr. Meredith; however, after a confrontation, Rosemary released Ellen from her side of the pledge. Realizing that Norman Douglas intended to marry her and that Rosemary also wished to marry, Ellen accepted Norman's proposal, agreeing to a double wedding alongside her sister.

_Sources: [v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008), [v5 c15 P30](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0030), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c21 P19](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0019), [v5 c21 P25](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0025), [v5 c22 P2](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0002), [v5 c22 P25](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0025), [v5 c22 P37](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0037), [v5 c22 P39](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0039), [v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012), [v5 c32 P23](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0023), [v5 c32 P29](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0029), [v5 c32 P39](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0039)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of a father who died when her sister was young  <sub>[v5 c21 P16](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0016)</sub>
- Belongs to a family of strong Episcopalians  <sub>[v5 c2 P64](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0064)</sub>
- Jilted by Norman Douglas in her youth after a foolish quarrel  <sub>[v5 c15 P30](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0030), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c22 P39](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0039)</sub>
- Made her sister Rosemary promise on their mother's Bible never to marry and leave her alone  <sub>[v5 c21 P25](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0025), [v5 c22 P25](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0025)</sub>

## Quotes

> Mark my words, Mr. Meredith, that man is going to fight somebody yet. He’s aching to. He is going to set the world on fire.  <sub>[v5 c13 P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027)</sub>

> I did not ask you for that promise. You offered it.  <sub>[v5 c22 P24](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0024)</sub>

> I have never found that Methodism was catching. And, as I was going to say when I was interrupted, badly as I felt, I did not give in to the Methodists.  <sub>[v5 c15 P4](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0004)</sub>
